title: Traditional Rigid Ductwork Installation: Assembly, Sealing, and Insulation
summary: This This Old House segment demonstrates a classic approach to installing rigid sheet-metal ductwork. It shows assembling two halves of rectangular duct, joining them with male/female connections using S-clips and drive cleats, and fastening with zip screws. It then covers sealing the seams with mastic products (mastic tape for longitudinal seams and elastomeric mastic for butt seams) and finally insulating the run with two-inch fiberglass insulation. The host notes the purpose of insulation in keeping conditioned air in the ducts and reducing energy loss, providing practical, step-by-step guidance on traditional duct installation.
topics: Tin knocking and nail alignment (male/female duct ends)
Bending with a metal brake for clean edges
S-clip use to couple duct pieces
Drive cleat positioning for joint strength
Sealing longitudinal seams with mastic tape
Sealing butt seams with elastomeric mastic
Applying tape over wet mastic seam areas
Insulation of duct with 2-inch fiberglass insulation
Importance of insulation for energy efficiency and correct heat/cool distribution

sections.description: Introduces the traditional rigid ductwork approach, explaining that ductwork typically arrives in two halves that are joined together. Demonstrates notching, bending with a brake, aligning S-clips, drive cleats, and securing with zip screws to create a solid, detachable joint.

sections.title: Sealing and securing seams
concepts: Longitudinal seam sealing with mastic tape
Butt seam sealing with elastomeric mastic
Taping over wet mastic areas to reinforce seal
sections.description: Shows how to create airtight duct runs by sealing all longitudinal seams with mastic tape and butt seams with elastomer mastic, then applying additional tape over the wet material to ensure a durable seal.

sections.title: Insulation and finishing
concepts: Pulling insulation snug and stapling to secure
Purpose of insulation: keep conditioned air and improve efficiency
sections.description: Covers installing 2-inch insulation around the duct, ensuring a snug fit, and securing it with staples. Explains why insulation is important for keeping heat or cooling where it belongs and for energy efficiency.
